title: A same-fraction-field DVR dominating a nonfield Noetherian local domain
statement:
Let $B$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] which is a local integral domain and not a field: $B
e0$, it has no zero divisors, and it has a unique maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_B
e0$. Let $K$ be a field [def-weil-field] containing $B$ such that every element of $K$ is $b/c$ with $b,c\in B$ and $c
e0$ (so $K=\operatorname{Frac}(B)$). Then there is a subring $A\subseteq K$ which is a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], contains $B$, has fraction field $K$, and satisfies $\mathfrak m_A\cap B=\mathfrak m_B$. Thus the inclusion $B\hookrightarrow A$ is local.

source.place: Tag 00PH, algebra-lemma-exists-dvr, specialized to the identity finitely generated field extension K/K.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-local-domain-birational-dimension-one] to the given inclusion $B\subseteq K$. Obtain $B\subseteq R\subseteq K$ with $R$ a Noetherian local integral domain of dimension $1$, fraction field $K$, and $\mathfrak m_R\cap B=\mathfrak m_B$. The hypotheses hold because $B$ is Noetherian and local and its nonzero maximal ideal excludes the field case.

source.place: Tag 00PH, algebra-lemma-exists-dvr, second paragraph of the proof; Tag 00P8, algebra-lemma-dominate-by-dimension-1.

proof.text: Let C be the integral closure of R in K [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. Apply [lem-sc-integral-closure-dedekind-surjective-fibres] to the identity finite field extension K/K to obtain IsDedekindDomain C. Mathlib integralClosure.isFractionRing_of_finite_extension identifies K as its fraction field. The integral inclusion R → C is injective because its composite into K is injective. Mathlib Algebra.IsIntegral.comap_surjective supplies a prime q of C whose contraction is the maximal ideal of R.

source.place: Tag 00PH, algebra-lemma-exists-dvr, final paragraph; Tag 09IG, algebra-lemma-integral-closure-Dedekind, statement and proof.

proof.text: The prime q is nonzero. Otherwise its contraction would be zero by injectivity of R → C, making the maximal ideal of R zero. A local ring with zero maximal ideal is a field, whose Krull dimension is zero, contrary to dim R = 1. No residue-field finiteness or separate proof of maximality of q is needed: the Dedekind localization theorem takes any nonzero prime.

source.place: Tag 031F, algebra-lemma-finite-extension-residue-fields-dimension-1, clause (1); Tag 00PH, algebra-lemma-exists-dvr, final paragraph.

proof.text: Use Mathlib Localization.subalgebra with the multiplicative set q.primeCompl to construct the localization A₀ directly as a C-subalgebra of K. This set lies in the non-zero-divisors because C is a domain and q is prime. The construction has the localization instance and fraction field K, implementing the fraction-field clause of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-normal-domain]. Apply [lem-sc-dedekind-localization-dvr] to the nonzero prime q of the Dedekind domain C to obtain that A₀ is a DVR. Restrict scalars through R and B to view exactly this subring as a B-subalgebra A of K.

source.place: Tag 00PH, algebra-lemma-exists-dvr, final sentence; Tag 00GY, algebra-lemma-localize-normal-domain; Tag 034X, algebra-lemma-characterize-Dedekind.

proof.text: Mathlib IsLocalization.AtPrime.under_maximalIdeal gives that the maximal ideal of A₀ contracts to q. Pull back along B → R → C → A₀, compose ideal comaps, and use q∩R = m_R and m_R∩B = m_B. The resulting equality m_A∩B = m_B gives IsLocalHom of the inclusion by Mathlib IsLocalRing.local_hom_TFAE. Restricting the base of the subalgebra does not change its ring or its specified inclusion into K, so its DVR and fraction-field structures give every asserted clause.

source.place: Tag 00PH, algebra-lemma-exists-dvr, final sentence; localization at a prime, Tag 07BH, local-rings paragraph.

proof_origin.place: Tag 00PH, proof specialized to L = K; dimension-one normalization by Tag 09IG. V8 Lean realization uses the nonzero-prime form of the Dedekind localization theorem, so the separate Tag 031F maximality step is unnecessary.
